title: KV spike-fidelity: p95 regression orchestrator and microburst fidelity harness
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Build a reproducible, CI-triggerable harness that can (1) simulate short-duration microbursts and long-tail traffic spikes against prefix/KV cache configurations, (2) sweep memory budgets to produce hit-rate vs p95 latency vs memory curves, and (3) detect regressions automatically using statistical change-point detection. This ticket owns the orchestrator and test workflows for fidelity-focused spikes (sub-second to multi-minute bursts) and integrates results into the performance dashboard and regression alerting pipeline. The harness must support both synthetic workload generation and trace replay from production token traces.
acceptance_criteria: Automated job that runs a phased spike suite (warmup, steady-state, microburst, cooldown) and emits tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, and hit-rate per step into Grafana/GCS.
Memory-stepped runs produce CSV artifact with hit-rate vs configured cache size vs p95 latency for each model profile (e.g., llama-13b, mix-quant profiles).
Regression detector flags a statistically significant p95 increase with an attached run diff and links to the failing workload and artifacts.
Jobs runnable in CI as 'kv-spike-fidelity' with a non-flaky baseline for <5% false-positive regression alerts on historical control data.
Documentation and runbook describing how to add new models, workloads, and cluster configs.
test_plan: Phase 0: unit tests for microburst injector and sample rate limiter (local docker-compose).
Phase 1: Synthetic workloads: exponential inter-arrival microburst generator (configurable burst length, tokensPerReq distribution, hot-key skew).
Phase 2: Trace replay: ingest production token traces, anonymize, and replay at different scale factors to simulate bursts and tail loads.
Phase 3: Memory-stepped sweep: run same workload across memory budgets [4GB, 8GB, 16GB, 32GB] and collect hit-rate/latency curves.
Phase 4: Regression job: compare new run to baseline using Bayesian online change-point detection + bootstrap of p95 to estimate significance and generate alert if delta > 10% with p<0.01.
Phase 5: CI gating: nightly baseline runs and PR gating for runtime and cache-related codepaths.
instrumentation: Emit tokens/sec, reqs/sec, backend queue length, tokenized request size, per-request KV cache lookup count.
Tag metrics with model_profile, cache_size_gb, shard_id, workload_id, trace_id.
Record per-request latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) and KV cache hit/miss counters with sample traces saved to GCS.
Attach memory pressure and eviction counts from runtime API to each run.
automation: Orchestrator: Kubernetes Job manifest generator that can spin up N driver pods and M runtime pods with perf hooks.
Collector: sidecar that aggregates histograms and writes canonical artifacts (CSV + ndjson traces) to GCS under /kv-fidelity-runs/<run-id>/.
Regression job: Lambda/Cloud Function that runs analysis on new artifacts, computes diffs vs baseline, and creates a GitHub issue or Slack alert when regression detected.
Runner wrapper: local CLI 'kv-fidelity run --profile microburst --mem 8G --scale 10' for on-demand investigations.
ci_integration: CI job kv-spike-fidelity (nightly + on-demand) lands artifacts to GCS and posts summary to #perf-alerts. PRs touching runtime cache eviction, prefetch, or kernel selection must include kv-spike-fidelity smoke run and a link to artifacts. Regression detector posts to Slack and files ENG issues when deltas exceed thresholds.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Trace replay may leak PII if anonymization incomplete. Mitigation: use existing anonymizer lib from infra (review by Security).
Risk: Nightly runs consume GPU quota. Mitigation: schedule to lower-cost region and use small model profiles for nightly baselines; reserve full-profile runs for weekly cadence.
Risk: Flaky detection due to natural variability. Mitigation: use Bayesian changepoint + bootstrap, require at least N=3 consistent runs before firing high-confidence incident.
